name: Demi Guard to Half Guard
summary: Demi Guard to Half Guard replaces a failing gi lapel-and-foot connection with a conventional one-leg trap while the bottom player keeps frames against the passer.
description: Demi Guard to Half Guard in gi BJJ: learn the starting controls, movement sequence, defensive reactions and recovery options for a connected lapel-guard exchange.
overview:
When the foot-on-lapel barrier stops managing pressure, the nearby leg may still be available for ordinary half guard. This recovery exchanges the special fabric control for a leg trap; it does not turn every loose Demi position into half guard automatically.

The defining Demi configuration is documented by [Legion](https://legionsandiego.com/the-jiu-jitsu-dictionary/#demi-guard). The half-guard recovery is a conservative connection between that configuration and [[Positions/Half Guard]], requiring the leg to remain within reach and frames to prevent a completed pass. Once half guard is established, its own underhook, back-take and submission routes require their usual controls.

attacker.name: Demi Guard to Half Guard Attacker
attacker.description: Execute Demi Guard to Half Guard with the right starting controls, a stable destination and a clear recovery when the attempt is blocked.
attacker.overview: You are underneath as Demi's lapel connection becomes unreliable. Recover a conventional leg trap while keeping your torso facing the passer. Release cloth that obstructs the change and retain frames; the recovery ends at half guard rather than at an immediate sweep or submission.
key_principles: Recognize loss of useful lapel tension early.
Keep frames while changing the legs.
Capture a reachable leg rather than stretching after it.
Release fabric that prevents a safe change.
setup_requirements: You begin in Demi Guard bottom.
The lapel or foot control is failing or no longer useful.
One opponent's leg remains between or within reach of your legs.
You can maintain frames that prevent a completed side-control pin.

execution_steps.description: Notice when the foot no longer has useful support from the lapel, before the passer clears both knees and reaches your torso.
Use the remaining upper-body frames and facing angle to preserve space for the legs to change without surrendering chest control.
Let go of lapel tension that binds your leg movement, keeping another frame in place rather than reaching after lost cloth.
Bring both legs around the reachable opponent's leg without turning against a knee that is still caught in fabric.
Confirm the one-leg trap and recover your side-facing posture with frames between the two upper bodies.
Assess the passer's posture and upper-body controls before pursuing the existing half-guard sweep, back-take or recovery options.

common_counters.counter: Keep the knee line outside the closing leg clamp
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_counters.counter: Contest the recovery while preserving base
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_counters.counter: Clear both legs and settle the pin
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_errors.error: Waiting until both knees have been passed
common_errors.consequence: No reachable leg remains for the intended recovery.
common_errors.correction: Start the change when the lapel barrier first becomes ineffective.

common_errors.consequence: The passer closes chest-to-chest space during the leg change.
common_errors.correction: Keep at least one effective frame while exchanging the controls.

common_errors.error: Clamping while the lapel still binds a knee
common_errors.consequence: The new trap can add tension to an already restricted joint.
common_errors.correction: Release the obstructing fabric before tightening the leg trap.

common_errors.error: Chasing a distant leg with straight arms
common_errors.consequence: The passer gains a path around your remaining barrier.
common_errors.correction: Keep your torso protected and recover a reachable guard.

common_errors.consequence: The opponent frees the leg during your premature reach.
common_errors.correction: Confirm the leg trap and posture before changing to offense.

training_progressions.description: You begin in Demi Guard bottom. With a cooperative partner, identify the required grips and leg contacts, then reset without applying pressure.
Perform the listed sequence slowly with a cooperative partner. Pause at the change of lapel or foot control and reset on any joint discomfort.
Let the partner use this response: Keep the knee line outside the closing leg clamp. Practice keeping a safe base or guard when it blocks the attempt, then reset.
Start at the stated origin with light resistance. Stop and reset at a stable destination, a counter, or a request to release; do not continue through a bound knee.

flashcards.question: What replaces the foot-on-lapel connection in this recovery?
flashcards.answer: A conventional half-guard trap around one opponent's leg replaces the failing fabric-supported barrier.

flashcards.question: When should you start recovering half guard from Demi?
flashcards.answer: Start when the lapel barrier stops working but the opponent's leg is still reachable and your frames can preserve space.

flashcards.question: What should your upper body keep during the leg change?
flashcards.answer: Keep protective frames and a facing angle so the passer cannot use the change to connect chest to chest.

flashcards.question: Why release fabric before tightening the half-guard trap?
flashcards.answer: Fabric that still binds a knee can obstruct the transition; release that tension before closing a new leg configuration.

flashcards.question: What must be checked before attacking from the recovered half guard?
flashcards.answer: Confirm that one opponent's leg is trapped and your posture and frames are stable before seeking a separate attack.

attacker.safety_considerations: Use controlled pressure with a cooperative partner when learning the lapel path. Release fabric immediately on a tap, verbal stop or discomfort. Do not rotate against a knee held by the lapel, and stop the drill when a stable landing is reached.

defender.name: Demi Guard to Half Guard Defender
defender.description: Recognize and respond to Demi Guard to Half Guard while protecting balance, remaining frames and a safe recovery route.
defender.overview: You are the passer trying to prevent the guard player from replacing the foot-on-lapel barrier with a leg trap. Track their knees and your controlled leg while keeping base. If they capture one leg between both of theirs, you must recognize the resulting half guard before continuing.
key_principles: Recognize the change of collar, lapel and foot controls early.
Keep a usable base or leg barrier while contesting the movement.
Choose a response that fits the current controls rather than a lost grip.
Release any connection that binds a knee during movement.
Identify the resulting position before continuing the exchange.
recognition_cues: The bottom player removes the foot from the lapel tail.
Both knees begin closing around one of your legs.
Their hands change from fabric control to frames protecting their torso.

defensive_options.action: Keep the knee line outside the closing leg clamp
defensive_options.when_to_use: Before both of the guard player's legs capture your leg
defensive_options.if_successful: The opponent must retain their existing Demi configuration.
defensive_options.risk: Pulling against uncleared fabric can bind your knee.

defensive_options.action: Contest the recovery while preserving base
defensive_options.when_to_use: As the guard player exchanges foot contact for a leg clamp
defensive_options.if_successful: The change stalls while the original guard remains contested.
defensive_options.risk: Overcommitting weight can give the opponent an elevation opportunity.

defensive_options.action: Clear both legs and settle the pin
defensive_options.when_to_use: When the opponent has released Demi without securing a leg trap
defensive_options.if_successful: You establish side control after denying the recovery.
defensive_options.risk: An incomplete clear leaves a conventional half guard.

favorable_outcomes.how: Keep the knee line outside the closing leg clamp. The opponent must retain their existing Demi configuration.
Contest the recovery while preserving base. The change stalls while the original guard remains contested.
Clear both legs and settle the pin. You establish side control after denying the recovery.

common_errors.error: Responding after the new controls are established
common_errors.consequence: The attacker completes the movement before the response affects it.
common_errors.correction: Recognize the listed cues during the control change.

common_errors.error: Turning against a knee still bound by the lapel
common_errors.consequence: The joint cannot follow the body movement freely.
common_errors.correction: Release binding tension and reset rather than forcing the turn.

common_errors.error: Ignoring the position left after the attempt
common_errors.consequence: You continue with a response intended for a guard that has already changed.
common_errors.correction: Check the actual leg and upper-body controls before the next action.

flashcards.question: What signals the Demi player is recovering half guard?
flashcards.answer: Their foot leaves the lapel tail and both legs move to capture one of your legs while the hands protect their torso.

flashcards.question: What remains if the opponent captures one leg after you clear the lapel?
flashcards.answer: You are in top half guard, so the leg extraction and upper-body control for a completed pass still need to be established.

flashcards.question: When can you complete side control during this recovery?
flashcards.answer: Complete it only when both the lapel barrier and the replacement leg trap have been denied and you have cleared the legs.

training_progressions.description: From the stated origin, have the partner begin slowly. Call out a listed recognition cue, then release and reset.
Keep the knee line outside the closing leg clamp. Use light resistance and stop when the response succeeds or the connection becomes uncomfortable.
Let the partner choose whether to continue or recover. Respond using the available controls; stop at the resulting stable position and name both players' roles.
